about.dev: Development build – not built by the updater.

backup.folderHint: copy via WinSCP or scp to {path}.
backup.intro: A backup from AMP or another panel (.zip). The panel detects game, version and the key settings, creates the server and then imports worlds, saves and configuration.
backup.noValues: No settings to prefill – the data itself is still imported.
backup.nothing: The panel found no game it can import in {file} ({entries} entries, {size}). Supported so far: Minecraft, ARK: Survival Ascended, Enshrouded and TeamSpeak 6.
backup.sizeHint: Uploading works up to a few GB. Use the import folder for larger backups.
backup.unsure: The panel is not sure which game this is. Please choose.
backup.willImport: Will be imported: {list} – {size}. Everything else in the archive is left alone.

create.prefilled: Fields marked “from the backup” were prefilled. Check, adjust, done.

disk.overLimit: Using more than assigned – increase disk space in the settings.

import.done: Import finished – the result is in the timeline.
import.folderHint: for large backups. Copy the file via WinSCP or scp to {path} on the panel VM.
import.intro: For example an AMP backup (.zip). The panel only looks for: {list} – everything else is left alone. Anything already here is first saved to the {folder} folder.
import.running: Import running. Progress and result are shown in the timeline. Start the server only afterwards.
import.title: Import backup
import.uploadHint: fine up to a few GB.

live.noAccess: You no longer have access to this server.

login.name: Username or email
login.tagline: All your game servers in one place
login.useApp: Sign in with app code instead
login.useRecovery: Phone not at hand? Use a recovery code

logs.liveHint: Keep reloading the newest file and jump to the new file when the game restarts
logs.none: No log files yet. They appear once the game has run.
logs.truncated: Showing the last {count} lines. Full file: download.

netcheck.clockFail: offset {s} s – too large. Epic then rejects sign-ins. Enable time sync on the VM (timedatectl set-ntp true).
netcheck.intro: Checks from the panel VM what games like ARK need for Epic Online Services: name resolution, HTTPS to Epic, which address the VM shows up with outside, and whether its clock is right.
netcheck.ipMismatch: {ip} – differs from the configured address {configured}. Epic lists the server under {ip}; players using the other address may not reach it.
netcheck.ipUnknown: {ip} (no IP configured above, so no comparison)
netcheck.title: Connection test

network.enterIp: Enter the public IP above (not a domain) and it will appear in the rules directly.
network.intro: The address players use to reach your servers, and which ports the panel hands out.
network.outside: Outside the range and therefore not reachable through the forwarding:
network.publicHostHint: Domain or IP you give to players – without port. Empty = the address you are using to open the panel.
network.rangeNote: Once a range is set, new servers only get ports from it. Existing servers keep their ports.
network.rulesHint: Add this once to {file} (in the same block as your other forwardings) so it survives a reboot. After that every new server is reachable from outside.
network.rulesNow: To apply it right away without a reboot, run these commands once on the host. Do not use {cmd} – it would add all existing forwardings a second time.
network.title: Network

ports.hint: Assigned by the panel. Extra ports are available in the container as NAME_PORT, e.g. DYNMAP_PORT.
ports.reallocateConfirm: Really new ports? The old address stops working
ports.reallocateHint: E.g. moves the server into the forwarded range.
ports.title: Ports

res.bandwidthHint: Applies to file uploads and downloads via the file manager.

server.notFound: This server does not exist or you have no access.
server.updateModpackConfirm: Do you want to update the modpack to version {version}? A backup will be created automatically before updating.
server.updateRestartNote: The 1-click update pulls the latest container image, updates the container, and updates the game files on start.
server.updatePreBackup: Automatically create a safety backup before updating (recommended)

servers.emptyCreate: Create your first one – pick a game, set RAM, done.
servers.emptyInvite: Once someone invites you to a server, it shows up here.
servers.title: Servers

settings.autoRestart: Auto-Start (Restart automatically up to 5× after a crash)
settings.autoRestartHint: Tries to restart the server up to 5 times after a crash. If it still crashes on the 5th attempt, it stays off and is shown as 'Unstartable' on the panel.
settings.gameHint: Same fields as when creating. Applies from the next start.
settings.name: Name
settings.resourcesLive: RAM and CPU can also be changed while running.
settings.runtimeHint: Must match the game version – e.g. Java 21 for Minecraft 1.21, Java 25 from 26.1.
settings.savedRestart: Saved. RAM and CPU apply immediately; Java memory adjusts on the next stop and start.
settings.stopFirst: Game settings, Java version and ports can only be changed while the server is stopped. Saves are kept.

status.autoStartHint: Automatically restarts the server up to 5 times on crash. After 5 failed attempts, it stays off as 'Unstartable'.
status.unstartableBanner: Unstartable: This server crashed 5 times in a row and was automatically turned off. Check the console or timeline for errors before starting it again.

backups.ignoreHint: Paths or patterns per line (e.g. *.log, temp, cache)
backups.lockedHint: Locked: Protected against automatic or accidental deletion
backups.mustStop: The server must be stopped before a backup can be restored.

backups.restoreConfirm: Do you really want to restore backup "{name}"? All current files on the server will be overwritten!

players.panelBans: This game has no readable ban list – shown are the bans issued through the panel.

motd.title: MOTD and server icon
motd.hint: How the server appears in the Minecraft server list. Click a color or format – it is inserted at the cursor, or around the selection.
motd.visibleChars: Visible characters – the server list cuts off beyond about 45
motd.stopFirst: Saving the MOTD works while stopped; the icon any time (applies after restart).

cover.hint: Shown on the tiles when creating a server and in the server list.
cover.title: Cover for {game}

pack.bannerFile: The file is uploaded into the server folder after creation. Start the server only after that.
pack.bannerText: Server type, pack and version are already set. RAM and Java match the pack – adjust here if needed.
pack.cf2: sign in with Google, GitHub or email and create a key under "API Keys" (free).
pack.cf3: Paste the key here. It is checked and stored encrypted; servers with CurseForge packs get it automatically.
pack.cfApp: Profile → ⋯ → "Export Profile" → upload the .zip below (needs the CurseForge key).
pack.cfAskAdmin: Ask an admin to set the CurseForge key.
pack.cfKeyNote: The key only leaves the panel towards CurseForge and is never shown in the interface.
pack.cfKeyReplace: Paste a new key to replace the old one
pack.confirm: Stop the server, create a backup, update and start again?
pack.ftb: Searched without sign-in. All FTB packs:
pack.ftbApp: Pick packs from the FTB App via the search above (source FTB) – same packs, no export needed.
pack.guideIntro: Search a modpack and click "Choose" – the panel sets server type, pack, version, Java and a RAM suggestion. On first start the server downloads all mods itself; depending on the pack this takes a few minutes.
pack.guideTitle: How it works – and where to find packs
pack.manualDownload: The author does not allow automatic downloads. Download the pack file by hand and upload it below as your own file.
pack.mcChange: This update changes Minecraft from {from} to {to}. Old worlds can break if mods are missing – the backup beforehand is your safety net.
pack.mr: Searched without sign-in. You can also browse packs on
pack.mrApp: Instance → ⋮ → "Export modpack" → upload the .mrpack file below.
pack.noCfKey: CurseForge is not searched because no API key is set – many big packs like All the Mods are only there. See the guide above.
pack.noEgg: The Minecraft Java game is missing from the catalog – it is required.
pack.noHits: Nothing found. Try another name or source.
pack.noRight: Updating needs the permissions "change settings" and "create backup".
pack.ownHint: .mrpack (Prism Launcher, Modrinth App) or .zip (CurseForge app). Uploaded into the server folder after creation.
pack.ownTitle: Your own pack from a launcher
pack.pinNote: The pack version is pinned, so the server does not silently jump to a new version on every restart – the panel shows updates and installs them with one click, with a backup first.
pack.prism: Select the instance → "Export" → "Modrinth (.mrpack)". Upload the file below.
pack.searchPlaceholder: Name or short name, e.g. atm10, cobblemon, stoneblock …
pack.unpinnedHint: The version is not pinned – the server silently installs the latest on every restart, without a backup. Pinning is recommended.
pack.updateNote: Steps: stop server → backup (must finish, otherwise nothing changes) → new version → restart. The backup is listed under "Backups".
pack.uploadFailed: Could not upload the pack file ({code}). Upload it via the file manager.

eggImport.catalogSearch: Search game in online catalog (e.g. Conan, DayZ, FiveM, Bungeecord) …
eggImport.catalogEmpty: No matching game found in catalog.
eggImport.catalogDirectUrl: Or paste direct GitHub JSON URL …
eggImport.hint: Own template or egg from Pterodactyl/Pelican – ports, ready pattern and permissions are adapted on import.
eggImport.notJson: The file is not valid JSON.

adminFiles.title: Files on the VM
adminFiles.intro: All panel folders: game data of every server, backups and NAS – like the instance folder in AMP. Administrators only, every change is written to the audit log.
adminFiles.warning: Changes take effect on the VM immediately. Do not delete or rename files of running servers, and only delete backups when you are sure.
adminFiles.readOnlyHint: This folder is mounted read-only. Files can be viewed and downloaded, but not modified.
adminFiles.serversHint: Files of installed servers are under "volumes" – one folder per server, labelled with its name.

hosts.title: Hosts
hosts.intro: Machines that run game servers: the local Docker host and connected NexusCores.
hosts.addIntro: Enter the address and token of the core. The core is checked right away - a wrong token is never stored.
hosts.name: Name
hosts.pinHint: The core's pairing PIN - confirms that token and core belong together
